root_idea.summary: The root centers on cutting, severing, or removing a portion of something.
root_idea.development: From the basic act of cutting, the lexicon develops meanings for cut branches, fresh fodder named for being cut, rods and implements, and figurative extensions such as breaking off speech or acting without preparation.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested noun قَضْب is also an appropriate classical citation form.

senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, it denotes fresh fodder, especially herbage cut for feeding; the term is also used collectively for such plants.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut or cut off something, including a branch or excess growth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A basic transitive use; the object may be cut from a larger thing or its redundant portions may be removed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike or beat someone with a rod or stick.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct Form I use with a person as the object and a rod or similar implement as the instrument.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To prune or cut the branches of a grapevine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional Form II use, especially for pruning in spring.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the sun, to extend or spread its rays like rods.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use describing the appearance of the sun's beams.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of land, to produce the plant called قَضْب abundantly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV intransitive use with the land as subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become cut or cut off.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive or passive-resultative Form VII use; it may be used intensively or of several things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become cut off or separated from one's companions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of being severed from a group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a star, to dart or shoot downward from its place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative astronomical or poetic use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut something off from the thing to which it belongs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VIII use retaining the physical sense of severing or breaking off.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To break off someone's discourse and turn it to another subject.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional rhetorical use: speech is abruptly cut off or diverted, sometimes with little connection to what preceded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To extemporize speech, a narrative, or poetry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression refers to producing words without prior preparation or elaboration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ride or take an animal before it has been trained or broken in.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of riding a young or untrained camel or other mount.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To task someone with work before he is able to perform it well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported lexical use connected with the cutting-derived idea of taking or imposing something before it has been prepared.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slaughter a camel while it is healthy, fat, and youthful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized figurative or conventional use applied to a camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tree whose branches grow long and lank.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical description of the tree's growth habit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tree or wood used for making bows, or an arrow shaft made from such wood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may refer to the source tree or to the resulting bow or arrow material.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A portion cut from a branch, especially for making a bow or arrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A cut piece or section of wood, distinct from the living plant from which it was taken.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A portion of a herd of camels, or of a flock or herd of sheep or goats.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective or distributive noun for part of a group of livestock.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Slender, light, or active.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival epithet applied to a she-camel and likewise to a man.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cut-off branch, rod, stick, wand, twig, switch, shoot, or stalk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The central nominal use refers especially to a branch cut from a tree; plural forms include قُضْبَان and قُضُب.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bow made from a rod or branch, especially one made from a branch that has not been split.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized object sense derived from the branch or rod meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The quill or shaft of a feather.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical or figurative extension of the slender rod sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The penis or virga of a man or animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical use of the rod-like noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slender arrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized weapon term based on the slender-rod shape.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slender sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative weapon term comparing the sword's form to a slender branch or rod.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An untrained or unbroken she-camel, and likewise an untrained male camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective can describe an animal ridden before it has become gentle or experienced in being trained.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The portions that fall from the ends of branches when trees or grapevines are lopped or pruned.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective term for the successive cut-off pieces produced by pruning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One whose habitual work or occupation is cutting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An occupational or habitual-agent noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plant name distinct from the fodder noun قَضْب.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tooth capable of cutting something apart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Appears in an idiom about having no tooth able to separate one half of a thing from the other.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who decisively settles affairs and is able to carry them out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative intensive epithet for a capable, action-oriented person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sword that cuts sharply; very sharp or sharply cutting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active-participial epithet for a sword, with intensified forms also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A reaping hook or pruning hook.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An instrument noun for cutting herbage or branches.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where قَضْب fodder grows, or where the trees used for bows grow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place noun covering either a fodder field or a stand of bow-making trees.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One whose craft or occupation is cutting, especially cutting herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An occupational agent noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land that produces the fresh fodder called قَضْب abundantly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive use for productive land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A classical Arabic poetic metre.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is explained through the idea of a metrical form cut off from another pattern.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Extemporized, when applied to verse, poetry, or writing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes material produced without prior preparation or composition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Untrained in a work, or tasked with it before being able to perform it well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use for something or someone not yet prepared or polished for the task.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Lexical sense retained despite unusual form attribution in the source text.

cautions: The Quran attests قَضْب only once, in 80:28, where the lexical evidence supports fresh fodder or herbage.

One Lane unit presents the sense 'to task someone before he can perform the work well' with an unusual form attribution; the semantic branch is retained, but its exact derivational vocalization is uncertain.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The lexical unit lane-unit:qDb:8521:g1:sub5 is under the اِقْتَضَبَ entry but prints قَضْبٌ alongside a verbal translation. Its meaning is represented as a Classical use, while the precise form attribution remains uncertain.
